subject: On‑prem deployment commercial — concession path & SOW redlines
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medisync.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@medisync.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — pricing and support

Mina — thanks again for the demo last week. The technical fit looks strong and our security team is comfortable with the VPC packaging you showed. Before we spin up legal/procurement, two quick commercial questions from our side: 

1) Platform fee amortization: can this be billed quarterly instead of up-front for a 24‑month pilot?
2) Support tiers: if we take the Standard SRE retainer instead of 24/7, do you offer a reduced platform fee?

We have a constrained FY budget but would like to start a pilot in Q3. I attached our PO template for reference.

Also — we expect a single public-cloud region initially (us-west). Let me know what flexibility you have on billing cadence and a plug‑in discount percentage for taking Standard support.

Oliver
Director, Platform Partnerships
Medisync Health

Attachments: Medisync_PO_template.pdf (stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medisync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — pricing and support

Thanks, Oliver — great to hear the security team is aligned. Short answers up front, then a suggested path: 

- Quarterly amortization: yes, we can structure the platform fee to bill quarterly for a 24‑month pilot (standard is annual up‑front). We would treat it as an amortized invoice schedule with a shortpaper SOW amendment.
- Support tier discount: we can offer a platform fee credit when choosing the Standard SRE retainer vs. 24/7. Typical credit sits between 8–15% depending on capacity commit.

Suggested concession path to get you started this quarter: 
- Pilot length: 24 months.
- Platform fee: $240k annual list (example). Offer: amortized quarterly payments (6 x $40k) for the first 12 months, then standard quarterly thereafter (schedule in SOW).
- Support tier: Standard SRE retainer at $40k/year; choose Standard and we apply a 12% platform fee credit for the pilot period.
- Capacity burst: include a 10% burst buffer for the first 90 days at no additional platform fee (to cover onboarding spikes).

I attached a redlined SOW with the above sketched in and the proposed invoice cadence. If that looks reasonable, we can (1) update DocuSign, (2) Marissa can confirm approval thresholds/discount authority, and (3) loop in procurement for contract review.

Next steps: please review the SOW_redlines and the amortization schedule I added on page 2. Happy to jump on a 30‑minute call to run through line items.

— Mina
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 415‑555‑0127

Attachments: Medisync_SOW_redlines.docx (summary redlines), Medisync_SOW_v1.pdf (original stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — pricing and support (internal)

Quick internal guidance on the concession path Mina proposed: 

1) Amortized billing: OK to approve for pilot but we should require a cancellation clause with a 90‑day notice plus a true‑up for usage if they exceed committed tokens by >25%.

2) Platform fee credit: 12% as an anchor is fine for Standard retainer. We should cap combined concessions (credit + onboarding burst) at 18% net to preserve book economics.

3) PO/legal: insist on our standard liability cap and data handling addendum; Irene can push legal to use our addendum instead of theirs.

4) Approval authority: Mina — you have authority up to 11% credit. Anything above that needs Marissa (me) approval. For execution speed, we can pre‑approve the amortized billing schedule but require doc signoff within 10 business days.

I'll draft a short executive summary for sales leadership if we want to move fast. Irene — can you confirm whether the liability carveouts on their PO are acceptable?

— Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales Operations

> Mina — great summary.

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medisync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Updated offer and next steps — Medisync pilot

Oliver — thanks for the quick review and the PO template. Based on our internal alignment, here's a formalized pilot offer we can put into the SOW: 

1) Pilot term & billing cadence
- Term: 24 months.
- Platform fee: $240,000/year list. For the pilot we will amortize the first 12 months across 4 quarterly invoices (6 x $40k over 18 months) — first invoice due on signing. (See SOW page 2 for payment schedule table.)

2) Support & credits
- Support: Standard SRE retainer at $40,000/year.
- Platform fee credit: 12% applied to the pilot platform fee if Standard is selected. Credit is reflected on quarter invoices as a line item.

3) Onboarding buffer
- We will grant a 10% burst buffer (token headroom) for the first 90 days for onboarding at no extra platform fee. Any sustained usage beyond headroom will follow the metered overage rates in the SOW.

4) Terms and legal
- We will not accept PO language that expands liability beyond our standard cap; please use the attached SOW and addendum. We can align on DocuSign for signatures.

Attachments included: Medisync_SOW_redlines.docx (redlines), Medisync_SOW_v1.pdf (clean copy). I also uploaded an execution copy to DocuSign; link below.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/EXAMPLE-DOCUSIGN-ID
HubSpot Deal: https://hubspot.example/contacts/12345/deal/RDW-4837

If this is in line with procurement's expectations, send the PO back as described and we will countersign same day. Otherwise flag any specific clauses you need changed and we'll triage with legal.

Best — Mina
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Mina/Marissa — this looks actionable and reasonable. Procurement reviewed the amortization schedule and prefers invoices on a true quarterly cadence; your cadence above is acceptable provided the first invoice is issued on signature. Attached is our PO (filled) and a short set of procurement comments — the only open items are (1) a minor liability carveout we asked to keep, and (2) a billing contact for invoices.

We can sign the DocuSign version if you confirm: 
- Billing contact: finance-ops@medisync.com
- Counterparty legal name as appears on PO: Medisync Health, Inc.

Once you confirm the billing contact and agree to the minor liability language (procurement suggested a clarification, not an expansion), we'll route to our CFO for signature. Appreciate the bandwidth to compress timelines here.

Oliver
